runs.summary: I read docs/api.md against shop/api.py, shop/export.py and shop/auth.py. The CSV columns and the error answer match the code. The "Who may call" sentence does not. I did not review the vendored Rail engine under .rail/; it is a third-party update.

findings.claim: The new text says only `api.delete_product` asks `shop/auth.py`, which is false. `api.rename_product` calls `auth.allowed(request, "rename")` and `api.delete_customer` calls `auth.allowed(request, "delete")`. Neither handler, nor `delete_product`, is in the handler table, so a reader cannot learn which handlers are role-gated. The new section also sits between the table and the `export.orders_csv()` paragraph, so the export paragraph now reads as part of 'Who may call'.

evidence.output:
delete_product: auth.allowed(request, "delete")
rename_product: auth.allowed(request, "rename")
delete_customer: auth.allowed(request, "delete")

findings.check: A doc-lint test that every public handler in shop/api.py is named in docs/api.md, and that each handler calling auth.allowed is listed as gated.
